entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease
entries.description: FDA today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds).
entries.summary: FDA approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets for treating neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease in adults and children weighing at least 15 kg.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must update labeling and patient eligibility criteria to incorporate this new therapy for GD3 patients.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide
entries.description: FDA  today announced the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP), a landmark initiative that will fundamentally transform how the FDA's regulatory drug and biologic approval decisions are leveraged by health authorities around the world.
entries.summary: FDA launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program, enabling other health authorities to rely on its drug and biologic approval decisions.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams worldwide must be aware that FDA approvals can now be used by foreign regulators, potentially impacting global development and approval strategies.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer
entries.description: FDA approved Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection, the first treatment shown to help people with a severe form of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) live longer.
entries.summary: FDA approved Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection for infantile‑onset Niemann‑Pick disease type C.
entries.why_it_matters: This approval introduces a new biologic therapy for a rare, severe pediatric disease, requiring RA teams to update labeling, reimbursement, and monitoring procedures.

entries.label: FDA
entries.title: FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
entries.description: FDA today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or a high-risk transient ischemic attack.
entries.summary: FDA approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa inhibitor to help prevent stroke in adults at high risk.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should incorporate this new drug into their stroke prevention formulary and consider potential interactions with antiplatelet therapy.

entries.title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherap
entries.summary: FDA granted accelerated approval for Rybrevant Faspro to treat adults with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must incorporate this new therapy into treatment protocols, update labeling, and monitor post‑approval safety.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Phased implementation of ICH M11: Clinical electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol (CeSHarP) – Notice to stakeholders
entries.description: This new guideline provides comprehensive clinical protocol organization with standardized content, with a Template which presents the format and structure of the protocol, including the table of contents, common headers, and contents; and a Technical Specification which presents the conformance, cardinality, and other technical attributes that enable the interoperable electronic exchange of protocol content.
entries.summary: The ICH M11 guideline introduces the CeSHarP framework for standardized, interoperable clinical protocol content.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must adapt protocol development processes to align with the new structured format and technical specifications.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice to stakeholders on implementing ICH M13B: Bioequivalence for immediate release solid oral dosage forms: Additional strengths biowaiver
entries.description: Part of the foreseen ICH M13 Guideline series (M13A-C), the ICH M13B Guideline is intended to provide recommendations on obtaining waivers of bioequivalence (BE) studies for one or more additional strengths of a drug product in an application where in vivo BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths. This guideline is applicable to both development and post approval phases for orally administered immediate-release (IR) solid oral dosage forms designed to deliver drugs to the systemic circulation, such as tablets, capsules, and granules/powders for oral suspension. The ICH M13B Guideline is the second Guideline in the foreseen series to describe the scientific and technical aspects of demonstrating BE for additional strengths of a drug product, i.e., obtaining waiver(s) for one or more strengths in an application with multiple strengths when BE has been demonstrated for at least one of the strengths following ICH M13A. How regulatory decisions may be made based on BE assessment is out of the scope of this guideline.
entries.summary: ICH M13B provides guidance on waiving bioequivalence studies for additional strengths of immediate‑release solid oral dosage forms when BE has been demonstrated for at least one strength.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing or approving multiple strengths of small‑molecule IR solid oral products must use this guideline to evaluate if BE waivers are applicable, potentially reducing study requirements.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: ICH guidelines implemented by Health Canada
entries.description: Health Canada has implemented and launched public consultations on several International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, reflecting Canada’s ongoing commitment to global regulatory harmonization. Stakeholders are encouraged to review and provide feedback on the draft guidelines for consultation by the respective deadlines, as Health Canada will forward all comments to the ICH for consideration in the finalization process. Health Canada has begun implementing finalized guidelines. Stakeholders are encouraged to integrate these guidelines into their drug registration processes.
entries.summary: Health Canada has launched public consultations on several ICH guidelines and has begun implementing finalized guidelines into its drug registration processes.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review the draft guidelines, provide feedback by the consultation deadlines, and incorporate the finalized guidelines into their registration submissions.

entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada granted a Notice of Compliance with Conditions for Calquence, authorizing its market launch pending additional clinical studies.
entries.why_it_matters: The RA team must monitor and ensure the sponsor completes the required studies to maintain compliance with the NOC conditions.

entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards.
entries.summary: FDA issued final guidance for cellular and gene therapy manufacturers to establish comprehensive, science- and risk-based potency plans.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing or overseeing CGT products must update their potency testing strategies and documentation to meet the new guidance requirements.

entries.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) for treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP).

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to incorporate this new biologic therapy into their regulatory strategy for RRP, ensuring labeling, post‑marketing commitments, and pharmacovigilance are updated.

entries.description: How to avoid delays when submitting clinical trial application assessments The UK's new clinical trial regulations came into force on 28 April 2026, introducing a more flexible and risk-proportionate approach to clinical trial assessment. Sponsors now submit a single clinical …
